toc.title: What GitHub adds to a Git repository

html:
1What GitHub adds to a Git repository

Git stores history. GitHub hosts Git repositories on a server and adds team features around them. The repository you push to is an ordinary Git remote, and in the lab a local bare repository stands in for it. The GitHub features come from the GitHub documentation and were not run, because they need an account.

Area Git alone GitHub adds
History Commits, branches, tags The same, kept on a server as the shared remote
Review Nothing built in Pull requests to propose, discuss and merge changes
Automation Nothing shared built in GitHub Actions workflows
Releases Tags Releases built on tags
Protection None Branch protection rules and rulesets
Security None Secret scanning, Dependabot alerts, push protection
Access Whoever can reach the path Accounts and permissions, for example write access to merge

GitHub names the default branch main in new repositories. You can change it in your settings, and changing it on an existing repository needs admin access. Locally, git init -b main gives the same name.

Tip

. Start local repositories with git init -b main. An older project on master can be renamed with git branch -m master main before the first push.

2Creating a repository

When you create a repository you choose its owner, its name and its visibility: public means everyone can see it, private means only the people you allow. GitHub also offers to add a README, a .gitignore template and a license. These community files are ordinary files, so they are versioned and reviewed like code.

File What it tells people
README What the project is and how to run it
LICENSE The terms under which others may use it
CONTRIBUTING How to propose a change
CODE_OF_CONDUCT How people are expected to behave
SECURITY How to report a vulnerability privately
.gitignore Which files Git must not track

Starting from an existing project. Create the GitHub repository empty. A README created there is a first commit that your local project lacks, and the two histories are unrelated.

Try it. The remote already has a commit, and the local project has its own.

git push -u origin main
git pull --no-rebase origin main

 ! [rejected]        main -> main (fetch first)
fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories

A plain git pull stops even earlier, with "Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches". The option --allow-unrelated-histories forces a merge, but an empty remote avoids the problem.

Tip

. Create the GitHub repository empty when you already have local work. Then the first git push -u origin main is a plain push.

3Clone URLs and authentication

Every repository has two kinds of URL to push to, and origin is the default remote name.

HTTPS SSH
URL form https://github.com/user/repo.git git@github.com:user/repo.git
How you log in A token, or a credential helper An SSH key
Prompts Fewer with a helper None once the key is set up

git remote set-url origin <url> switches a remote between the two.

Try it. Switch the same remote to the SSH form. This does not contact GitHub.

git remote add origin https://github.com/ada/shopfront.git
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:ada/shopfront.git
git remote -v

origin	git@github.com:ada/shopfront.git (fetch)
origin	git@github.com:ada/shopfront.git (push)

Password authentication for Git on the command line is gone. Use a personal access token, a credential helper such as Git Credential Manager, or SSH. A credential helper stores your login so Git does not ask every time; Git reads it from the credential.helper setting.

GitHub recommends fine-grained tokens over classic whenever possible. Unused tokens are removed after one year.

Fine-grained token Classic token
Reach One resource owner, selected repositories Every repository you can reach
Permissions Granular The repo scope for command line Git
Public repos you do not belong to Cannot contribute The only type with write access
Limits Up to 50 per user; an organization may need to approve Not recommended when a fine-grained token works
Tip

. Never put a token in a remote URL. The lab showed it stored in plain text in .git/config and printed by git remote -v.

SSH keys. A key is a pair: a private file that stays on your machine and a .pub file that you give to GitHub. ssh-keygen -t ed25519 creates both. SSH keys avoid prompts, can also sign commits, and inactive ones are deleted after one year. To test a key, the usual command is ssh -T git@github.com. It needs your account, so it is not run here.

Try it. Generate a key in the current folder. For real use, accept the default location and set a passphrase. The empty one (-N "") is only for this demo.

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "ada@example.com" -f ./id_ed25519 -N ""
ls id_ed25519*
ssh-keygen -l -f id_ed25519.pub

Your identification has been saved in ./id_ed25519
Your public key has been saved in ./id_ed25519.pub
id_ed25519
id_ed25519.pub
256 SHA256:zGHGreCb/AqnG15gTNmJLdud/aScZJpiFTn1v24VtW4 ada@example.com (ED25519)
Tip

. Share the .pub file and never the private key. The public file is one line that starts with ssh-ed25519.

4Forks, branches and upstream

A fork is a separate repository, owned by you, with its own branches, issues, pull requests, Actions and settings. GitHub shows the original, the upstream, under the fork's name. Any public repository can be forked, a private one only if the owner allows, and the fork's visibility follows the upstream.

Branch Fork
Lives in The same repository Your own repository
Needs write access to the original Yes No
Typical user A team member An outside contributor
Remotes origin only origin (your fork) and upstream (the original)

GitHub describes two models: fork and pull, where contributors fork the upstream, and shared repository, where collaborators push topic branches. After cloning your fork, add the original as a second remote called upstream. To update the fork, use GitHub's website sync option, or use Git: git fetch upstream, then a merge or a rebase.

Try it. Bring Ada's fork up to date. The lab uses a second bare repository as the fork.

git remote add upstream ../octo_up.git
git fetch upstream
git log --oneline main..upstream/main
git merge --ff-only upstream/main
git push origin main

 * [new branch]      main       -> upstream/main
c8c557a Add search
Fast-forward
   9f01c82..c8c557a  main -> main

A branch such as fix-typo pushed to the fork is not in the upstream. When the upstream moves on, rebase that branch onto upstream/main and push it with --force-with-lease.

Tip

. Keep main of your fork clean and work on branches. Then git merge --ff-only upstream/main always succeeds.

5The GitHub CLI

gh is GitHub's command line tool, separate from Git, and one more way to sign in. The commands below are named here and were not run in this course.

Task Command
Sign in gh auth login
Create a repository gh repo create
Clone a repository gh repo clone <owner>/<repo>
Fork a repository gh repo fork
Open a pull request gh pr create
Merge a pull request gh pr merge

6Practice Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Ada has a local project and creates a GitHub repository with a README. Her first git push is rejected, and a pull says "refusing to merge unrelated histories". Why?

  • AThe remote has a first commit that her project lacks
  • BHer token does not include the repo scope yet
  • CThe remote branch is named master and not main
  • DHer local project has no commits to push yet
Show the answer

Answer: A. The README is a commit with no relation to her history, so an empty repository would have avoided it.

S2git push over HTTPS asks for a password, and her account password is refused. What is the right fix?

  • AReinstall Git so that password login works again
  • BRename the remote from origin to upstream instead
  • CSwitch the default branch name from main to master
  • DUse a personal access token or a credential helper
Show the answer

Answer: D. Password authentication for Git on the command line was removed, so you use a token, a helper or SSH.

S3ssh-keygen -t ed25519 wrote id_ed25519 and id_ed25519.pub. Which file does Ada add to her GitHub account?

  • Aid_ed25519, the private key file
  • BBoth files, packed into one archive
  • Cid_ed25519.pub, the public key file
  • DThe fingerprint line, typed by hand
Show the answer

Answer: C. The public file is meant to be shared, and the private key never leaves your machine.

S4Ada cloned her fork, and git remote -v shows only origin. The original project has new commits. What does she do first?

  • ARun git pull origin main to get the new commits
  • BAdd the original with git remote add upstream
  • CDelete the fork and create a new fork again
  • DRun git push --force so the fork matches
Show the answer

Answer: B. The new commits are in the original repository, so she needs a remote that points at it before she can fetch.

S5Cy has no write access to the team's repository but wants to propose a fix. Which model fits?

  • APush a topic branch straight to the team repository
  • BAsk for a classic token and push to the team's main
  • CFork the repository and propose the change from it
  • DClone the repository and rename its default branch
Show the answer

Answer: C. In the fork and pull model, contributors work in their own fork and propose changes back to the upstream.

S6A teammate ran git remote add origin https://ada:TOKEN@github.com/ada/shopfront.git. What is the problem?

  • AHTTPS URLs cannot contain a user name or token at all
  • BGit deletes the token again after the first push
  • CThe remote name must be upstream when tokens are used
  • DThe token is stored in plain text in .git/config
Show the answer

Answer: D. The URL is saved as written, so anyone who reads the config file or the git remote -v output sees the token.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does GitHub name the default branch of a new repository?

Show the answer

main.

R2Which two URL types can you use to push to a GitHub repository?

Show the answer

HTTPS and SSH.

R3Which token type does GitHub recommend whenever possible?

Show the answer

Fine-grained personal access tokens.

R4Which command creates an ed25519 SSH key pair?

Show the answer

ssh-keygen -t ed25519.

R5What is the usual name of the remote that points at the original repository of a fork?

Show the answer

upstream.

R6Which two steps update a fork's main from the original with Git?

Show the answer

git fetch upstream, then a merge or rebase of upstream/main.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
GitHub adds pull requests, Actions, releases on tags, protection, security features, accounts and permissions
Default branch main in new repositories; locally git init -b main
New repository choose visibility; create it empty when you push an existing project
Community files README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SECURITY, .gitignore
URLs HTTPS https://github.com/user/repo.git; SSH git@github.com:user/repo.git; git remote set-url
Login no passwords; token, credential helper or SSH; fine-grained tokens preferred
SSH key ssh-keygen -t ed25519; share the .pub only
Fork separate repository; remotes origin and upstream; git fetch upstream then merge or rebase
GitHub CLI gh auth login, gh repo create, gh repo fork, gh pr create, gh pr merge (named, not run)
